subject.title: [Security] Unsafe deserialization of incoming WebSocket commands in Gateway

question: Does any current Gateway request path copy or merge attacker-controlled prototype-named properties into a prototype-bearing target after frame validation, making this an exploitable security boundary?
rationale: The report is security-protected, but raw JSON parsing alone does not establish prototype pollution and the proposed affected architecture differs from current main; an owner must confirm or reject the missing source-to-sink link.

options.title: Request a concrete sink proof
options.body: Keep the report open while asking for a minimal frame and downstream operation that demonstrably modifies a target prototype on current main.

options.title: Close as unsupported
options.body: Close the report after owner confirmation that all relevant paths validate or consume values without an unsafe assignment or merge sink.

options.title: Add defense in depth
options.body: Adopt restricted-key rejection only if maintainers intentionally want a broader Gateway input policy independent of demonstrated exploitability.
